historical_record.description: The Guilfoy Cornice Works Building went up here in 1924, a one-storey shop with a mezzanine, 50 feet by 165, for a fabricator of architectural sheet metal that worked in it until 1985.
Seventeen feet were cut from the back of the Guilfoy Cornice Works Building and a new front built on Natoma Street.
A vacant, light-industrial building totaling 8,250 gross square feet stood at the property.
The City Planning Commission certified the Final Environmental Impact Report for the project at 1234 Howard Street.
